title: 5G SPACE USER TERMINAL (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7A.080) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. The activity will:- Review and consolidate the connectivity use cases of 3GPP networks in exploration missions (Moon and/or Mars)- Identify potential future exploration missions- Define and study architecture and scenarios of 5G cellular networks that could provide connectivity and enhanced navigation.- Design and implement an engineering model of 5G user equipment, including a test equipment, for connectivity in exploration missions.- Test the connectivity and positioning performance of the 3GPP networks using the developed test equipment.- Develop a roadmap to reach a flight model with integration of LunaNet navigation receiver capabilities

title: Acquisition d’un système complet d’échosondeur multifaisceaux
description: Un système hydrographique multifaisceaux de dernière génération est recherché pour la mesure précise des fonds aquatiques. L’objectif est l’acquisition d’un système intégré composé d’un sonar multifaisceaux, d’un logiciel d’acquisition performant, ainsi que d’un système de navigation inertielle (INS) assisté par GNSS. Le système doit répondre aux exigences les plus élevées en matière de précision, de stabilité et de flexibilité, et être adapté à une utilisation dans des environnements maritimes et limniques exigeants (Moselle). Les spécifications techniques ci-dessous définissent les exigences minimales pour le système à fournir. Les soumissionnaires sont invités à détailler dans leur offre en quoi leur solution répond ou dépasse les caractéristiques demandées. Un seul fabricant doit être choisi pour l’ensemble du système, comprenant le sonar multifaisceaux, le logiciel d’acquisition et le système INS. title: SEPARATION SYSTEM FOR STACKED HIGH ASPECT RATIO SATCOM SATELLITES ( ON REQUEST) (ARTES AT 4E.099) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and verify an Open Standard of a separation system specifically for stackedhigh aspect ratio satellites (up to 1,200 kg class spacecraft).Targeted Improvements:Enabling technology for launches of stackedhigh aspect ratio satellites.Description: High aspect ratio satellites are an established form factor for satcom satellites, already operating and providing global telecommunication services. To maximise launch capacity, it is common to launch large stacks of multiple (10s) of such satellites together. The required separation technologies have to date been bespoke developments by and for eachspecific constellation. In Europe, there is currently no such system available, nor an off the shelf existing solution.This activity aims to develop an open standard for a European hold down and release system to enable stacked launches of up to 60 high aspectratio (up to 1200kg class) satellites. This will ensure that development of such systems is coordinated across Europe and allow different providers to be mixed within single launches and across multiplelaunches and constellations. A separation system by necessity includes: a mechanical load path for the stack, the hold down mechanism, a pre-loading device to ensure that the stack is effectivelyheld down through launch conditions. a release mechanism and a sequencing system to control the ejection of each spacecraft fromthestack. The engineeringmodel separation system concept will be developed, and a breadboard will be manufactured and tested in asufficiently representative scenario to validate critical functions of the system in the different stacking configurations. Then, an engineering model will be manufactured and tested, including a series of deployment tests in different conditions to assessthe overalldesign performance. The final stage of the activity will propose an open standard for separation system for stacked high aspect ratio satcom satellites to promote compatibility of spacecraft design.

title: RECEIVER TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR PNT SOLUTIONS WITH ONLY 1 AND 2 LEO SATELLITES IN VIEW - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested.
